summary: Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist and religious studies. A graduate student at the University of Chicago in 1991, she held posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell (~2001), Professor at Harvard, and Pali Text Society Regional Representative (2026).

Anne MacDonald specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Lambert Schmithausen, Karin Preisendanz, and Geshe Tashi Namgyal. She held posts at Vienna, Hamburg, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied under John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. Her career includes posts at Smith College (1988–1989), Tokyo National Research Institute (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist, religious, and historical studies, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and has held associate and full professorships at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012, 2026).

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein, Dagpo Rinpoche, Yonten Gyatso, and Geshe Ngawang Dakpa. She held appointments at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, including as editorial consultant in 1982 and attested in 2003.

Anne-Marie Esnoul (1908–1996) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and EPHE under Paul Masson-Oursel, she held posts at CNRS (~1946–1952), EPHE (~1961–1978), and the Institut de civilisation indienne.
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist. She completed her studies at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1962), Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a scholar of religion, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler, she held professorships at Marburg, Ankara (1954–1967), and Harvard (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1925–1930) and later held posts at Humboldt (~1935–1946) and the University of Hamburg (~1950–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher. She studied at the University of Otago (~1947–1952) and earned her PhD at Somerville College in 1952. She later held academic posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Christian Lindtner, David Seyfort Ruegg, at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989), and earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna by 2002.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg. Her career includes posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1999), Humboldt University (attested 2021), and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Annie Montaut is a linguist and Indologist who studied under Nicole Balbir. She held posts at Normal Higher School of Tunis (1974–1976), Queen's University (1977–1980), Jawaharlal Nehru University (1981–1987), Paris Nanterre (1988–1990), and INALCO (1990–2014).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, where he served as a professor from ~1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2001–2007) and has served as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~2013).

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (1910–1993) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving there as a lecturer in Chinese (1946) and professor (1956–1975) succeeding Duyvendak.

Anthony Kennedy Warder (1924–2013) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough and William Stede, later serving as Lecturer at Edinburgh (1955–1963) and Department of East Asian Studies Chairman at Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Bristol and Oxford under Paul Williams, Steven Collins, and Alexis Sanderson, he held posts at the University of Montana (attested 1997) and the University of Arizona (attested 2020).
Anthony W. Barber works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and later held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).
Antoine Lutz studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela and earned his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University.
